brief: A portable electronics organizer: a base with removable bins for small parts, at least one drawer, and a carry handle.

requirements.evidence: piece:-1,0,0;full and piece:0,0,0;full provide a connected two-cell base (level 0). check_build ok true, meshClash clear.

No bin parts installed (counts: piece 2, notch 1). Sockets for hex-bin-full / div2 / div3 etc. are available at both base cells (s313-s360) but none have been placed, so no removable storage for small parts is present.

notch:0#-1,1#notch1 with stem hex-drawer-frame-notch-fm is installed in the notch between the two bases. This is the notch drawer-frame (a drawer bay), but no family:drawer insert (family drawer sockets on a half-base cut face or slide/swing/long) is present; find_sockets drawer returns 0, so a functional pull-out drawer is not verified.
No cover and no handle installed. find_sockets handle returns 0 and find_sockets cover shows s353/s354 still empty; a handle requires a cover on its face, so carry functionality is absent.

finish.summary: Current build is two full hex bases with a notch drawer-frame (hex-drawer-frame-notch-fm) between them. check_build is ok and meshClash clear with only informational OPEN_CAP_FACE warnings. It provides a base and a drawer bay, but has no removable bins and no carry handle/cover, so it only partially meets the portable electronics organizer brief.

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
